C-STABILIZE-CHECKBOX-DIRTY.Summary: Preserve the already working one-revision checkbox dirty/close path while repairing one-step task undo and blocked readonly checkbox edits. Route editable checkbox clicks exactly once to their dedicated content-state handler; do not then add a generic click cursor/history snapshot. Cancel checkbox default actions on explicit readonly Muya surfaces.
C-STABILIZE-CHECKBOX-DIRTY.ApprovalBasis: Owner-approved RECOVERY and delegated recommended safety decisions, 2026-11-09. The coordinator explicitly requested actual built-renderer proof before repairing checkbox-only edits, one semantic revision/cascade, unsaved close protection, undo/redo and readonly/mirror safety; approved compact C-STABILIZE-CHECKBOX-DIRTY if a defect was confirmed. This bounded repair addresses proven history and readonly failures, not an invented missing change notification. No release or publication authorization.
C-STABILIZE-CHECKBOX-DIRTY.BaselineEvidence: On clean faab503, built-renderer Chromium and WebKit both confirmed saved task clicks update Markdown, isSaved=false and contentRevision exactly once and open the real unsaved-close dialog. Both engines failed one-step undo for single and autoCheck-cascaded tasks and allowed a locked checkbox to mutate Markdown. No dispatchChange addition is justified: native input already supplies the single dirty event.

Goals.Goal: One task click or nested autoCheck cascade remains one semantic dirty revision and is undone/redone in one document-history operation.
Locked/readonly and mirror checkbox clicks do not mutate Markdown, dirty/revision state or checkbox DOM.
Actual close-command cancellation preserves the checkbox edit; existing native input notification is retained exactly once.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep source changes in clickEvent.js checkbox routing; preserve clickCtrl/history/renderer store behavior and all unrelated pointer actions.
Use synthetic saved files and Auto Save off; no real user document, dependency install, commit/push, product-tree edit or release operation.
Use port 4187 and two workers in a dedicated portable test config; reuse no foreign preview; preserve timeout and assertion strictness.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No global undo redesign, extra dispatchChange, split integration, profile/lock architecture rewrite, security or release changes.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Built Chromium and WebKit tests prove single/cascade checkbox Markdown + one revision + dirty marking, actual unsaved close protection, one undo and redo.
Readonly/locked and existing read-only mirror clicks leave content/revision/dirty and checked state unchanged.
Focused routing unit controls preserve editable single routing, native input once, readonly cancellation and noncheckbox generic routing; existing keyboard undo, close and lock suites remain green.
Current graph/verification and local contracts describe the routing boundary; final command gates and post-archive integrity/status are recorded.

AffectedAreas.Area: M-012 checkbox/native click routing and history ownership; M-011 renderer dirty/close boundary verified without implementation change.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npm run build && CI=1 npx --no-install playwright test --config tests/e2e/checkbox.playwright.config.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Red-to-green real browser cases from faab503; report that the suspected dirty-loss path already passed instead of claiming it was fixed. Verify the actual confirmed undo and readonly defects. Preserve a portable public config and private raw receipts.

C-STABILIZE-CHECKBOX-DIRTY.FactualCorrection: 2026-11-09, coordinator-confirmed finite evidence correction: earlier explanatory prose attributed the existing change notification to native input. Actual built Chromium/WebKit task clicks reach the existing keyboard.dispatchEditorState click listener and its scheduled dispatchChange; no DOM input event is observed at the measured editor boundary. The user invariant remains one semantic store change/revision per single or nested cascade, correct close protection and undo/redo, and readonly safety. The browser diagnostic now counts actual LISTEN_FOR_CONTENT_CHANGE deliveries plus contentRevision (both exactly one), preserving all original user requirements, source scopes, assertion targets, tasks and command gates. The failed invented input-count receipt remains privately retained as checkbox-grace-final.log; this is a factual correction, not a new product requirement or lifecycle successor.
